title: security: under the PROTECTED profile, repository content (.moe/project.json settings.agentCommand) chooses the binary the agent wrapper runs on the host
description:
architect-4ae016fb flagged this in RF05 rev 2 (task-b439d7fb) as an unowned R01 gap: the R01 memory names it "agentCommand and WSL/native sessions under strong", nominally R10's, and no open row covers it. The human approved filing it as HIGH on 2026-10-30.

What the code does
- moe-jetbrains TerminalAgentLauncher.kt:267-268 resolves the command as `agentCommand ?: <project state>.settings.agentCommand ?: "claude"`. The project state comes from .moe/project.json, which is repository content. The value goes to the wrapper as --command / -Command (buildBashCommand, buildWslBashCommand, buildPowerShellCommand), with no check of RuntimeSelectionPolicy.profile, so it applies under RuntimeProfile.PROTECTED too.
- scripts/moe-agent.sh (~360-440) parses --command into a binary and argv, then runs it. The basename only classifies codex, gemini or grok; anything else is treated as claude. There is no allowlist. Check the ps1 twin.

Why it is in scope
RF05's threat model puts repository content in scope, including ignored .moe files a pull can overwrite, and rules that a file under the project may add a refusal but never an admission. Choosing which binary runs on the host is an admission.

Required
Under PROTECTED, the agent binary a seat runs must not be selectable by repository content. The architect picks the mechanism, for example IDE-level user settings, or a fixed set of known agent CLIs resolved from trusted locations. Cover both wrappers. VS Code parity can be a follow-up row. Decide whether RF07 (task-f3f364a6) should dependsOn this row.
definitionOfDone: Under RuntimeProfile.PROTECTED, the JetBrains launch path never hands a repository-supplied agent command to the wrapper. A ./gradlew test case covers a project.json that names a non-standard command.

Under PROTECTED, moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 refuse to run an agent binary chosen by repository content, with a message naming the rejected command. Launcher tests cover it, and scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes.
Legacy (non-protected) behavior is unchanged, or the change is documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

implementationPlan.description:
In moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/TerminalAgentLauncher.kt:

1. Add `internal sealed interface AgentCommandChoice { data class Run(val command: String); data class Refused(val message: String) }`. The known set is `AgentProvider.entries.filter { it != AgentProvider.CUSTOM }.map { it.command }` (~:144), so the menu's providers and the guard cannot drift apart.
2. Add `internal fun agentCommandFor(profile, explicit, projectSetting): AgentCommandChoice`.
   - LEGACY: return Run(explicit ?: projectSetting ?: "claude") exactly as today.
   - PROTECTED: candidate = (explicit ?: projectSetting)?.trim() ?: "claude".
     - Run(candidate) only when it is in the known set.
     - Otherwise Refused("Protected execution profile: the agent command '<value>' (<from .moe/project.json settings.agentCommand | custom command>) is not one of claude, codex, gemini, grok, so no agent was started. Pick an agent from the Agents menu.").
     - Truncate the value to 200 characters and replace control characters, matching the wrapper's MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_COMMAND_REFUSED rule.
3. resolveContext (~:224) currently has `val resolvedCommand = agentCommand ?: MoeProjectService...settings?.agentCommand ?: "claude"`. Replace it:
   - the profile is PROTECTED exactly when `selected != null`; do not read project.json a second time;
   - call agentCommandFor(...);
   - on Refused, Messages.showErrorDialog(project, message, "Moe") and return null, so no terminal and no wrapper start;
   - on Run, use its command.

Change nothing else: the legacy branches, the CUSTOM menu flow, the stored custom command and buildCommand stay as they are. Under PROTECTED, a user-typed custom command is refused at launch with the same dialog, because the wrapper (task-aa85ff13) would refuse it anyway.

Error handling: the decision is pure and never throws. A null basePath is still handled by the existing early return. Run TerminalAgentLauncherTest until it is green.

Nothing else changed (CUSTOM flow, buildCommand, legacy branches). - Ignoring project.json's agentCommand entirely under PROTECTED: rejected. The IDE settings dialog writes agentCommand into project.json, so honoring a known name keeps that working. A non-standard value refuses, which is fail-closed and visible, rather than silently falling back to claude.

- One row covering both slices: rejected for size (6+ files, two harnesses). The wrapper files are also serialized behind CQ-R13c2 and many other wrapper rows, so the wrapper half is task-aa85ff13.
